# gt birds due: print the late daily reports and the exact request to send (gt-m0shy) [closed task P2]

## Description

## Goal
One command, gt birds due, prints which reporters' daily reports are due or stale and, for each, the exact request to send, so the overseer's 30-minute check runs one command instead of remembering the process. The request text moves from ~/gt/.runtime/overseer/birds/daily-profile.txt into the gastown repo (docs/birds/daily-request.md) as the single source.

## Constraints
- Go with unit tests: internal/cmd (gt birds due) reading the same reporter list and daily.json files as the bird_reports patrol (share one small package, internal/birdreports, that both use).
- Output: one line per due reporter with its age, then the request text with <NAME> replaced; exit 0 when nothing is due, exit 1 when any is due (so a prompt can branch on it). The request text file is embedded with go:embed.
- Update ~/.claude/docs/overseer-check-prompt.md in the same change set is NOT possible from a rig; instead state in the bead comment the one line the overseer adds there. Do not edit ~/.claude.
- No sending: the command prints, the overseer sends with SendMessage.

## Out of scope
The patrol (the sibling bead), the dashboard page, publishing artifacts.

## Gate
go test ./internal/birdreports and go test ./internal/cmd -run BirdsDue.

## Size
one worker, one landing

## Acceptance

- [x] internal/birdreports reads a reporter's daily.json written_at and reports fresh, stale or missing against an injected clock. Run: go test ./internal/birdreports
- [x] gt birds due prints one line per due reporter and the request text with the name filled in, exits 1 when any are due and 0 when none. Run: go test ./internal/cmd -run BirdsDue
- [x] docs/birds/daily-request.md holds the request text (the eight sections of the DAILY profile, the daily.json fields, the fixed slug) and the command embeds it; a test fails if the file is empty. Run: go test ./internal/birdreports -run Embedded

## Acceptance

# lint: parse the optional ## Interfaces section (gt-hgt9j.14) [closed task P2]

## Description

## Goal
Parse an optional `## Interfaces` section so the epic-level lint can compare the names beads define and use. The section holds `Defines:` and `Uses:` lines, each a comma-separated list of identifiers. This bead only parses; the graph checks come later (docs/plans/2026-11-03-bead-lint-v2-design.md, decision 3).

## Constraints
Create internal/specdispatch/graph.go and create internal/specdispatch/graph_test.go. Use the existing Sections helper in internal/specdispatch/lint.go to find the section (key `interfaces`); do not write a second section splitter. Exact names:
```go
type InterfacesBlock struct { Defines, Uses []string }
// ParseInterfaces returns (block, present, err). present is false when the bead has no Interfaces section (not an error). A line that is not blank, not "Defines: ..." and not "Uses: ..." is an error naming the 1-based line within the section and its text. Each list item is trimmed and must be an identifier: letters, digits, underscore and dot, starting with a letter or underscore (a dot allows Type.Method); anything else is an error naming the item. Repeated lines of one kind merge, in order, without duplicates.
func ParseInterfaces(description string) (InterfacesBlock, bool, error)
```
A leading `- ` bullet and backticks around an item are stripped. Bead gt-hgt9j.12 must have landed; the K1 bead before this one in the chain edits lint.go, so it lands first.

## Out of scope
The graph checks, the command, and the lint verdict.

## Gate
`go test ./internal/specdispatch -run 'InterfacesParse' -count=1`.

## Size
One worker, one landing, about 20 minutes.

## Acceptance

- [x] TestInterfacesParseDefinesAndUses: both line kinds parse into the two lists in order
- [x] TestInterfacesParseRejectsBadLine: a line `Provides: X` returns an error naming the line number and text
- [x] TestInterfacesParseRejectsNonIdentifier: an item `3rd` or `a b` returns an error naming the item, and `Store.Mutate` is accepted
- [x] TestInterfacesParseAbsentSection: no Interfaces section returns present false and a nil error
- [x] TestInterfacesParseMergesRepeatedLines: two Defines lines merge without duplicates

## Acceptance

- [x] TestInterfacesParseDefinesAndUses: both line kinds parse into the two lists in order

- [x] TestInterfacesParseRejectsNonIdentifier: an item `3rd` or `a b` returns an error naming the item, and `Store.Mutate` is accepted
- [x] TestInterfacesParseAbsentSection: no Interfaces section returns present false and a nil error
- [x] TestInterfacesParseMergesRepeatedLines: two Defines lines merge without duplicates
